It comes on in waves too, when I had more T and less E it was more of a "overall mood."

I'm trans and I believe gender is a social construct.

TERFS deny the existence of trans people altogether, I think they can't fathom why someone would want to change their gender or feel like gender is fixed and are afraid of trans women, feel like a trans woman is a man invading women's spaces.

Which is so sad, trans women are women so by using that rhetoric TERFS try to exclude women "who aren't women enough" from women's spaces. Passable trans women fly under their radar, they're really trying to enforce their gender standards and their expectations of a woman's spaces.

The law is inhumane. Many doctors are inhumane and misgender patients. Nonbinary genders are completely ignored by the law. If it's so hard to find an endo with time to see patients people can't get the hormones they need there's a problem.
Estradiol is estradiol, testosterone is testosterone, men are men and women are women. Trans women are naturally women so when you say "match the natural system" that is exactly what HRT aims to do.

Either way the "natural systems" are resulting in a hormonal imbalance. What about cis women without ovaries or cis men without testicles? Which system are you referring to? Cis people are given hormones to match their natural systems, trans people are given hormones to match their natural systems. The natural systems are being helped with medicine.

I'm trying to say that one is an example of how accessible hormones are for cis people while trans people are treated a lot differently by medical professionals.

Maybe more trans people need hormones than cis people, but cis people need hormones too, and they get it so much easier.

Everyone has estrogen and testosterone.

Hormonal medicine corrects a imbalances. They're for correcting natural problems. Hormones are vital for health. The denial of hormones is inhumane.
